learning: If oscillation stays above 0.34 on the oval, damping is the lever, not geometry. If progress falls below 0.85 at y=0.07, the row is too far ahead for the straights. If s-bend and slalom max_error stay at 0.061 or above, bend exits are not sensing-limited.
notes: Builder's y=0.07 geometry with a moderately more damped controller (kp 2.1, kd 0.35). Read the race against iteration 3 (203.20), which had the same controller family at y=0.06.
rationale: The Builder's y=0.07 proposal is the single change under test: the five 16 mm sensors move from y=0.06 to y=0.07 with x and footprint unchanged. Earlier sensing has been the only geometry lever that moved the oval (iterations 2 to 3: max_error 0.0617 to 0.0598, progress 0.53 to 0.87). The cost showed up in the controller: oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.339 at iteration 3 (kp 2.2, kd 0.30). Moving the row forward effectively raises loop gain, so jitter is likely to rise further, not fall. Iteration 4 softened the controller (kp 2.0, kd 0.35) but also widened the outer pair, so it is confounded. It moved oscillation only to 0.333, which says a small change is not enough. I therefore keep the Builder's geometry exactly and make a moderate damping change: kp 2.2 to 2.1 and kd 0.30 to 0.35. The slightly lower kp offsets the extra gain from the forward row, and the higher kd damps the jitter. ki stays 0 to avoid wind-up on bends. base_speed stays at 1.2, because progress has been limited by off-track exits, not speed. Line loss stays last_direction, since every loss has been a bend exit. Expected result: oval progress at or above 0.85 and oscillation at or below about 0.34. Bend exits may stay near 0.061, since they have not moved across geometries since iteration 2.
